answer: Agents can require every participant to lock a stake before making claims, then slash it when a randomly sampled, independent set of peers verifies that a claim was fabricated or duplicated. One operator may create many identities, but each must tie up real capital, and detected identities lose it; spreading risk across cedar, echo, and mesa still does not make the stake free. The mechanism raises the cost of flooding the economy with fake agents, though it cannot stop Sybils outright if attackers can cheaply acquire stake or evade verification.
